1004755.etyen:
From mat (“food”) + gjerd (“act, deed; making, preparation”), literally “food-making” or “food preparation”. The first element is from Old Norse matr (“food”), from Proto-Germanic *matiz, from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d- (“food”). The second element is from Old Norse gerð (“act, deed; preparation”), from Proto-Germanic *garwidō (“preparation”), related to *garwijaną (“to prepare”).
The regional form majel is a dialectal reduction of the compound.

en.g: selection thinning, dominant thinning, thinning from above; a thinning method in which mainly tall or dominant trees are removed to improve the growing conditions of smaller, vigorous trees
x: I en høytynning er det hovedsakelig i det øverste kronesjiktet det tynnes
In a high thinning, thinning is carried out mainly in the upper crown layer.

1005011.etyen:
Compound of høy (“high, upper”) + tynning (“thinning”), literally “high thinning”.
The first part høy (“high”) continues Middle Norwegian høg (“high”), under East Nordic influence, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *hauhaz (“high”), from Proto-Indo-European *kewk- (“high, elevated”). The last part tynning (“thinning”) is derived from tynn (“thin”) with -ing (“action/result-forming noun suffix”); tynn is from Old Norse þunnr (“thin”), from Proto-Germanic *þunnuz (“thin”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ténh₂us (“thin”), from *ten- (“to stretch”).
